Slides 2 and 3 pass cleanly — 2 names the concept directly (a count + a function, 'lenses to read with'); 3 is a claim-shaped discipline header matching the corpus precedent shape ('Passing is not proof'-style). Slide 1 is the closest call: rule 4 explicitly lists 'The question' among its empty-container failure-mode examples, and this header is a question. Distinguishing test: 'The question' is a bare article+noun label that could sit atop any Q&A slide in any file and names nothing on its own; 'What would have caught this earlier?' is a full, specific interrogative — it names the diagnostic ACT itself (retrospective catch-point identification), which per the backing block IS this file's entire content ('the driving question... deliberately a question rather than a checklist', backing L66). Covering the bullets, a reader still walks away holding the actual question, not a pointer to one described elsewhere. Truth clause: all three headers assert only what their bullets support — no dropped qualifiers, no unsupported universals, no category errors. No two headers share a concept; none is an orphan-mystery or pure-position header.
